keyVerseText: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon.
rootMeaning: The name אֱלִידָד (ʼĔlîydâd) derives from the same root as אֶלְדָּד (ʼEldâd), meaning "God of (his) love" or "my God has loved." This etymology highlights a personal and relational aspect of God as one who loves and is the source of love. The root conveys more than a simple name; it expresses a deep theological truth about God's affectionate and covenantal relationship with His people.
usageInScripture: The word אֱלִידָד (ʼĔlîydâd) appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Numbers 34:21, where it is translated as "Elidad." The consistent translation of this proper noun as a personal name indicates its function as an identifier rather than a descriptive term. Its singular occurrence as the name of a Benjamite chief involved in the land allotment underscores its historical and tribal significance without ambiguity in meaning.
theologicalSignificance: The original meaning of אֱלִידָד as "my God has loved" enriches our understanding of biblical names as carriers of divine truth and personal testimony. This name reminds believers that God’s love is foundational to His covenant relationship with Israel, shaping their identity and inheritance. In the Christian faith, this reflects the unchanging love of God revealed ultimately in Christ, who embodies God’s love for His people. Recognizing such names deepens our appreciation for how Scripture communicates God's character through history and personal identity.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 34:21 identifies Elidad as "the son of Chislon" from the tribe of Benjamin, marking him as a leader responsible for apportioning the Promised Land. The presence of the name Elidad here not only situates the individual historically but also implicitly reminds readers of God's loving provision and guidance in distributing the land. The meaning "my God has loved" enriches the verse by linking the practical task of land division to the theological reality of God’s love sustaining and directing His people.
